To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inspection efficiency of a sample inspection plan is a function of two parameters, the proportion of the population that is nonconforming, and the proportion of nonconforming items in the sample that are correctly identified.

the published sampling inspection plans, which are based on the assumption that the sampling operation is completely efficient (i.e., all inspected items are classified correctly), are not valid when the inspection operation is not completely efficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating the parameters of a binomial distribution from a single sample of size n.
determining the effect of inspection error on the guarantees of the sampling inspection plans.
the development of a sampling plan that is based on the assumption of imperfect inspection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the plans should not be used unless the inspection operation is known to be efficient.
the plans are not valid when inspection error is present, and that the only safe course is to assume the worst possible error rate.
the published plans are not valid in the presence of error.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sampling inspection plans are not invalidated in the presence of a reasonable amount of inspection error.

the plans are valid in the sense that they give an upper limit to the probability of rejection of a lot of good items, but that they do not give a lower limit to the probability that a bad lot will be accepted.
the inspection error does not materially affect the validity of the published sampling inspection plans for most cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the published plans should be used only as a first step in the process of determining the sampling plan for any given situation, and that the sampling plan should be adjusted to reflect the efficiency of inspection in the specific situation.
, for most inspection plans, the probability of acceptance for a batch of items with quality below that of the sampling plan is not significantly affected by the presence of inspection errors.
, for a given level of inspection error, the sampling inspection plans provide a guarantee of the quality of the product which is much better than that of the 100% inspection plans.
